newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's troops kill three in Kinshasa protest.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's troops kill three in Kinshasa protest.

text.p: Three people were shot dead by soldiers in Kinshasa on Friday during a protest by about 1,000 opposition activists over President Laurent Kabila's banning of political activity, witnesses said.

The soldiers opened fire after the demonstrators from the radical PALU party loyal to the memory of nationalist independence leader Patrice Lumumba tried to regroup after being dispersed by police, witnesses added.
Kabila took power and renamed Zaire the Democratic Republic of the Congo after his forces toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.
Kabila banned all political activity, including protest marches by opposition parties, shortly after taking power. He has also given himself wide-ranging powers as president.
Most opposition protests to date have featured supporters or allies of veteran Mobutu opponent Etienne Tshisekedi, the main political opposition leader in the former Zaire.
Troops broke up early protests by firing in the air. They allowed some subsequent marches to take place without intervening.
Soldiers took Tshisekedi away for questioning on June 26, after he defied the ban to address students. They released him the next day.
Witnesses reported five injured among Friday's demonstrators, who had been marching from the central railway station to the presidency.
Police fired into the air in an attempt to disperse the crowd in front of the presidency, causing the marchers to flee in panic and then regroup near the foreign ministry, where soldiers opened fire.
Supporters of PALU, the Unified Lumumbist Party led by veteran opposition leader Antoine Gizenga, staged a protest in 1995 under Mobutu during which at least 10 people were killed.
